input: Set up a bird feeder in the backyard

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the feeder is already purchased or still needs to be bought determines whether the plan starts with shopping or straight with installation.
If this is meant to attract specific birds (e.g., hummingbirds, songbirds, woodpeckers), the feeder type, placement, and feed choice all change significantly.
The specific backyard conditions — trees, fences, open ground — determine where and how the feeder can be mounted or hung.
A budget limit affects which feeder style and feed type are realistic options, especially if a pole, hook, or mounting hardware is also needed.
Some people want a DIY/natural look, others want a polished store-bought setup — this shapes product and placement recommendations.
The mounting method (hanging from a branch, pole-mounted, window-mounted, fence-attached) is the single most decisive physical step and depends on what the yard allows.

Success could mean simply having the feeder up, or it could mean actively seeing birds visit within a certain timeframe — this determines whether the plan stops at installation or includes attracting and maintaining bird activity.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a bird feeder in the backyard
gold.taskDescription: Install and stock a bird feeder in the backyard so it is ready to attract birds.

questions.title: Do you already own a feeder, or buy one too?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan includes a shopping/selection phase or jumps straight to installation.

questions.title: What types of birds are you hoping to attract?
questions.description: The target bird species dictates the feeder style (tube, platform, suet cage, nectar) and the type of seed or food to stock.

questions.title: What structures exist to hang or mount it on?
questions.description: Knowing whether there are trees, a fence, an eave, or open ground shapes the mounting method and any hardware needed.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this project?
questions.description: A budget ceiling affects feeder quality, feed quantity, and whether additional hardware like a pole or squirrel baffle is feasible.

questions.title: Do you prefer a natural DIY look or store-bought finish?
questions.description: Style preference guides whether to recommend rustic wooden feeders, sleek plastic/metal ones, or a homemade option.

questions.title: How do you plan to mount it — hung, pole, or fixed?
questions.description: The mounting method is the core physical action of setup and determines tools and hardware required.

questions.title: Is the goal just installed, or actively visited by birds?
questions.description: Defines whether the plan ends at physical setup or extends to tips for attracting birds, maintenance schedules, and refilling routines.
